pool.name: DLL AI, Data & Semantic Systems Pool
pool.description: Decision Loop Labs test pool: AI architecture, LLM and agent engineering, semantic modelling, data architecture, MLOps, AI governance and applied research at five fictitious organizations.

organizations.name: Lumen Semantic Labs GmbH
organizations.description: Builds a knowledge platform for engineering-heavy manufacturers: it ingests specifications, test reports and service tickets, links them in a domain knowledge graph and answers engineers' questions with cited, retrieval-grounded LLM responses. Customers run it in their own cloud tenants.

organizations.name: Northbeam Analytics AB
organizations.description: Operates a managed data and forecasting platform for utilities and grocery retailers: smart-meter and point-of-sale streams, a lakehouse, and demand forecasts that feed grid balancing and store replenishment.

organizations.name: Veritas Clinical AI SAS
organizations.description: Develops CE-marked clinical NLP software that extracts structured findings from radiology and pathology reports for hospital registries and trials. Every model release passes a documented clinical validation.

organizations.name: Orbisure Insurance Group
organizations.description: Composite insurer in Central and Eastern Europe automating claims intake and underwriting support with machine learning and LLM agents, under the EU AI Act, Solvency II and national supervisory expectations.

organizations.name: Helix Robotics Research Ltd
organizations.description: Research company building learning-based manipulation for warehouse robots: vision-language models for task understanding, imitation and reinforcement learning, and sim-to-real transfer, with a small production team taking results to pilot sites.

roles.title: AI Systems Architect
roles.description: You own the end-to-end architecture of Lumen's answering system: document ingestion and chunking, the hybrid retrieval layer (BM25, dense vectors and graph traversal), model routing between hosted and customer-deployed LLMs, citation verification, and the evaluation harness that decides whether a change ships. You make the trade-offs explicit — latency versus grounding quality, cost per answer, tenant isolation, what runs on-premise — and record them as architecture decisions. You work with the knowledge-graph, retrieval and platform teams, review their designs, and present the architecture to customers' security and IT architecture boards. This is an architecture role with hands-on prototyping, not a research position.

roles.title: Knowledge Graph Engineer
roles.description: The knowledge graph links parts, requirements, test results and failure reports across a customer's documents. You build and run it: modelling entity and relation types with domain experts, implementing extraction and entity-resolution pipelines that populate the graph from documents and PLM exports, writing graph queries the answering system uses for multi-hop questions, and keeping the graph consistent when sources change. The graph runs on Neo4j today with an RDF export for customers who integrate it with their own ontologies. Engineering rigour matters: provenance on every edge, incremental updates, measurable precision of extracted relations.

roles.title: Semantic Systems Engineer – Ontology & Vocabulary
roles.description: Customers describe the same thing in many ways: a 'bearing failure', 'Lagerschaden' and part number 4711-B. You design the semantic layer that makes them comparable: ontologies and controlled vocabularies per customer domain, alignment between customer taxonomies and Lumen's core model, and the rules that let the knowledge graph and the retrieval layer use them. You work closely with customer domain experts in workshops, keep vocabularies versioned and testable, and measure how alignment changes answer quality. This is a modelling role first: precision in definitions and the patience to reconcile experts' mental models count more than writing large amounts of code.

roles.title: LLM Engineer – Retrieval & Answering
roles.description: You implement the parts of the answering pipeline that turn retrieved context into reliable, cited answers: prompt and context construction, structured outputs, citation alignment, refusal behaviour when evidence is missing, and fine-tuning of small rerankers and answer models for customer deployments. You run experiments against the evaluation harness, ship changes behind flags, and debug failure cases reported by customers down to the retrieved chunks. The role is implementation-heavy: you own production code paths and their performance, not the overall architecture.

roles.title: Data Architect – Lakehouse
roles.description: Northbeam's lakehouse ingests 4 billion meter readings and 300 million retail transactions a day. As Data Architect you define how data is modelled, stored and governed: the medallion layers on Delta Lake, domain-oriented data products with clear ownership, contracts between producing and consuming teams, retention and partitioning strategy, and the semantic layer that analysts and forecasting models share. You decide when streaming is worth its cost, set standards for data quality checks, and guide the migration of a legacy warehouse. You work across data engineering, ML and customer analytics teams and with the DPO on personal data in smart-meter streams.

roles.title: Data Engineer – Streaming Ingestion
roles.description: Smart meters report every 15 minutes, and late or duplicate readings are normal. You build and operate the ingestion pipelines that turn these streams into clean, deduplicated, time-aligned tables: Kafka topics, Flink jobs with event-time windows and watermarks, schema evolution with a registry, and backfills when a utility sends corrected data. You own pipeline SLAs, alerting and the runbooks, and you work with the data architect on table design. Practical streaming experience and careful handling of time are the core of this role.

roles.title: MLOps Engineer
roles.description: Northbeam trains around 2,000 forecasting models a night, one per grid area and store cluster. You build the platform that makes this routine: orchestrated training pipelines, a model registry with lineage to data snapshots, automated validation gates before promotion, batch and online serving, and monitoring for data drift and forecast degradation. You work with data scientists to turn notebooks into reproducible pipelines and with the platform team on Kubernetes and GPU capacity. You care about boring, repeatable releases of models.

roles.title: Machine Learning Engineer – Demand Forecasting
roles.description: You improve the forecasts that decide how much bread a store bakes and how much reserve power a grid operator buys. You design features from weather, calendars, promotions and meter history; build and compare gradient-boosting and deep-learning forecasters; quantify uncertainty with probabilistic forecasts; and work with customers' planners to understand which errors are expensive. You implement models in production code with the MLOps team and own their evaluation, including backtests that reflect how forecasts are actually used.

roles.title: Clinical NLP Engineer
roles.description: Radiology and pathology reports are dense, abbreviated and written in French, German and English. You build the models that extract findings, measurements and negations from them into structured registry fields: annotation guidelines with clinicians, transformer-based extraction models, rule components where they are more reliable, and error analysis against annotated test sets. Your code becomes part of a CE-marked product, so you document data provenance and model changes for the quality system. Clinical background is not required; care with language and evaluation is.

roles.title: AI Quality & Clinical Validation Engineer
roles.description: Before a model version reaches a hospital it must be shown to be safe and effective for its intended use. You design and run that evidence: validation protocols with clinical partners, stratified test sets by site, scanner vendor and language, statistical analysis of performance and subgroup gaps, and the validation reports that go into the technical documentation. You also run post-market performance monitoring and decide, with the clinical lead, when drift requires action. You are the person who says 'not yet' with data.

roles.title: AI Governance Specialist
roles.description: Orbisure runs more than 40 models in pricing, claims and fraud, plus new LLM agents in claims intake. You build and run the governance that keeps them lawful and controllable: the AI inventory and risk classification under the EU AI Act, model risk management standards with the second line, documentation and transparency requirements, human-oversight design for automated decisions, and the review board where new use cases are approved. You translate regulation into concrete controls teams can implement, and you check that they did. Technical literacy is needed to challenge model owners; you are not expected to build models yourself.

roles.title: Agentic AI Engineer – Claims Intake
roles.description: A claim arrives as an email with photos, a police report and a policy number. You build the agent system that reads it, asks the customer for missing information, checks coverage against policy data through tools, and prepares a case for a human handler — never deciding the claim on its own. You design tool interfaces and their permissions, plan-and-execute loops with explicit stop conditions, audit trails for every step, and evaluation scenarios that include adversarial and incomplete claims. You work with the AI governance specialist on oversight and with claims handlers on where automation actually helps.

roles.title: Data Scientist – Underwriting Risk Models
roles.description: Commercial property underwriting at Orbisure relies on risk scores that combine building data, hazard maps and loss history. You develop and maintain these models: generalised linear models and gradient boosting with monotonic constraints, explanations underwriters can use, and the model documentation the model risk function reviews. You partner with actuaries on loss data and with underwriters on what an interpretable score must show. Interpretability and documentation are as important here as predictive power.

roles.title: Applied AI Research Engineer – Vision-Language Manipulation
roles.description: Helix's robots must understand instructions like 'move the damaged boxes to the returns cart'. You research and engineer the models that ground such instructions in what the robot sees: vision-language models adapted to warehouse scenes, policies conditioned on language, and data collection strategies that make them robust. You read and reproduce papers, run large training jobs, design ablations that answer real questions, and hand working results to the production team. Publications are welcome but the measure of success is a robot that completes more tasks.

roles.title: Machine Learning Engineer – Simulation & Sim-to-Real
roles.description: Most of Helix's training data comes from simulation. You build the simulation and data pipeline that makes it useful: physically plausible warehouse scenes in Isaac Sim or MuJoCo, domain randomisation, synthetic data generation at scale, and the evaluation that compares simulated and real-world success rates. You work at the boundary between research and engineering, turning researchers' experiment code into reliable infrastructure and finding out why a policy that works in simulation fails on the pilot site.

roles.title: Perception Engineer – Production Robots
roles.description: At pilot sites the robots must find, segment and pick thousands of different parcels under changing light. You own the production perception stack: detection and segmentation models optimised for edge GPUs, calibration of multi-camera rigs, latency budgets, and the monitoring that flags when a site's conditions drift. You integrate research models into a deterministic, testable pipeline and keep it running at 99.5 % pick readiness. Strong C++ and Python, and experience shipping vision to real hardware, are the core.
